title: ISM Services PMI (Dec 2026 data) — the January edition, on the FOURTH business day
source: EST: ISM's own release-schedule paragraph, re-read verbatim on 2026-09-05 from the August-2026 ISM Services PMI report (PRNewswire, dateline Tempe, Ariz., 2026-09-03, 10:00 ET): 'The full text version of the ISM(R) Services PMI(R) Report is posted on ISM(R)'s website at www.ismrob.org on the third business day* of every month after 10:00 a.m. ET. The one exception is in January, the report is released on the fourth business day of the month. *Unless the New York Stock Exchange is closed.' January 2027's business days begin Mon 2027-01-04 (2027-01-01 is a Friday holiday), so the fourth is Thu 2027-01-07 — the identical arithmetic that produced the on-record 2026-01-07 release (2026-01-01 Thu holiday, then Fri 01-02, Mon 01-05, Tue 01-06, Wed 01-07). Derived off the NYSE trading calendar, the rule reproduces all nine 2026 ISM Services release dates 9/9 with nothing left over. ismworld.org was probed direct 2026-09-05 and returned a 922-byte Google-reCAPTCHA challenge on its ROB-calendar path and HTTP 400 on its Report-On-Business path, so no 2027 schedule could be read; this is a rule-derived date and nothing more, checked 2026-09-05
notes: DISCOVERED during the ism-services-2027-02-03 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-05). Proposed for one specific reason beyond coverage: this is the report that PROMOTES ism-services-2027-02-03 from estimate to a primary-sourced date, because every ISM Services report names its successor verbatim one edition ahead (the 2026-09-03 report names 'Monday, October 5, 2026'). That promotion is registered as FT-ism-services-2027-02-03-1, scored 2027-01-08. Fills the same year-boundary gap as its manufacturing sibling: this calendar tracked ISM services monthly through 2026-12-03 and then stopped at the 2026 boundary rather than at any analytical judgement. Filed at impact high to match the five existing services entries. READ IT, DO NOT TRADE IT — the ism-services-2026-11-04 research measured all eight 2026 releases and found release-day moves in TLT/^TNX/SPY/QQQ/XLF/IWM statistically nil; ism-services-2026-12-03 added that the 10:00 ET release hour is quieter than an ordinary hour in four of five instruments; and ism-services-2027-02-03 tested that null out of sample on 2026-09-03, the year's largest services beat (PMI 55.4 vs 54.1 consensus, Prices 72.6 vs 70.0), where TLT moved +0.15% (18th percentile of its own 2026 distribution) and the ten-year yield FELL 0.71%. Note the date shape: this is the one edition each year that does NOT publish on the third business day, and this session's cross-series work found the services release-day bond effect real but small (^TNX clears its own-year p78 on 34.8% of 132 releases, p = 7.0e-4) and its month-slot cells uninformative at n=11. AMENDED 2026-09-05 by this event's own initial research (docs/research/events/ism-services-2027-01-07.md), which changes two things. (1) The January fourth-business-day arm of the rule — previously resting on the single on-record 2026-01-07 — now reproduces 4/4 against independently datestamped releases (2017-01-06, 2019-01-07, 2020-01-07, 2026-01-07), and this date's own promotion trigger is the 2026-12-03 report, which by ISM's one-edition-ahead convention should name it verbatim (FT-ism-services-2027-01-07-1, scored 2026-12-04) — earlier and more direct than the 2027-01-08 scoring of the sibling registration above. (2) The bond-effect line quoted above no longer stands: run against the 528 other early-month (1st-5th trading day) sessions instead of a 22% construction baseline, ^TNX is 37.1% vs 30.1% (p = 0.121) and TLT 31.1% vs 30.5% (p = 0.899), ^TNX clears more often on D-2 than on the release, and 2026 rejected the pooled rate 0-for-9 out of sample. The surviving fact is an early-month calendar effect, not an ISM one. What keeps this entry valuable is structural: a plus-or-minus-5-day corridor over 249 entries containing ZERO tracked events, outside the 2027-01-16 blackout and ~19 sessions after the 2026-12-09 FOMC, which makes it the cleanest observation of the measured null this chain will get — and therefore the print it must not pre-trade.
